findings.title: codemie log unaware of new notice level
findings.problem: The Logger gained a new 'notice' level, but src/cli/commands/log/types.ts's LogLevel union is still 'debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error', and parser.ts's normalizeLogLevel() has no branch for 'notice' so it falls through to `return 'debug'`.
findings.impact: In the codemie log viewer, notice-scoped hook-failure entries are silently reclassified as debug: LogFilterEngine.byLevel's { debug:0, info:1, warn:2, error:3 } map means `codemie log --level warn` or `--level error` will not show them, and formatter.ts's formatLevel() falls into its 'debug'/default case, rendering them dim blue 'DEBUG' instead of a warning color — directly undermining this change's stated goal of making hook failures clear to users inspecting their logs.
findings.recommendation: Add 'notice' to the LogLevel union, give it a branch in normalizeLogLevel() and a level-rank entry in LogFilterEngine.byLevel (above warn, since it is meant to always surface), and a distinct color case in formatter.ts's formatLevel().

findings.title: Hook-failure notice() has no rate limiting
findings.problem: executeSingleHook's catch block calls `logger.notice(...)` unconditionally on every invocation; there is no per-hook or per-session dedup/throttling before the console.warn fires (executor.ts already has a hashHook() helper at line 366, but it is not used to gate notice()).
findings.impact: A hook that fails on every PreToolUse/PostToolUse call (e.g. a broken hook script) will print a fresh yellow ⚠ banner to the console on every single tool invocation for the rest of the session, defeating the goal of making hook failures clear rather than noisy.
findings.recommendation: Needs a human decision on the throttling shape (once per hook-hash per session vs. time-windowed vs. count-capped) before implementing; not a mechanical fix given no spec guidance on the desired behavior.

findings.title: notice() drops extra console args
findings.problem: notice(message, ...args) passes ...args into writeToLogFile('notice', message, ...args) (line 348), so extra args reach the file log, but the console.warn call at line 354 only interpolates `message` and never spreads ...args into the console call.
findings.impact: Any future caller of logger.notice() that passes extra arguments (the current two call sites only pass a single pre-interpolated string, so the bug is latent today) will see those args recorded in the log file but silently missing from what the user sees on the terminal — the two output channels diverge for a method whose whole purpose is guaranteed console visibility.
findings.recommendation: Spread ...args into the console.warn call the same way writeToLogFile does, e.g. `console.warn(chalk.yellow(...), ...args)`.

findings.title: Shared static CODEMIE_HOME risks worker races
findings.problem: testCodemieHome = join(tmpdir(), 'codemie-test-home') is one fixed path shared by all three vitest projects (unit/cli/agent) and every test file within them, with no per-worker or per-run uniqueness suffix — this is the literal approved spec design (business_review item 1, pass), not an oversight.
findings.impact: Vitest runs test files across parallel workers; any test relying on the config-level default CODEMIE_HOME (rather than mkdtemp'ing its own, as codex.reconciliation.test.ts and the new isolation-focused tests already do) that performs real file I/O under that path risks colliding with a concurrent worker on the same directory. Reachability of an actual collision (which specific non-overriding tests write real files there) could not be fully confirmed from source within the review budget, so this keeps its lens-derived severity rather than being downgraded.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the spec owner whether the shared-path design already assumes no non-overriding test performs concurrent file I/O there, or whether the path should get a per-worker/per-PID suffix (as the edge-case lens's guard_snippet suggests) to remove the race risk outright.
